title.script_alignment: Identical 2005 purchases introduce two financial paths. A leftover nail and family photo contrast with a financed kitchen renovation. Extra principal payments face repeated moves in 2010 and 2020, with transaction fees and low-rate borrowing used to explain divergence. The 2026 balance and foregone-fee calculation put a number on the tradeoff. Driving past the first home reveals a mature tree, turning uninterrupted time into an emotional metaphor. The final reflection asks what a larger home cannot replace. Pronouns shift between neighbors and alternate selves, and payoff descriptions conflict. The stored ending is complete; actual delivery is unverified.
